project.name: luxio
project.description: Luxio is an Angular-based web assistant application with AI chat, code editor, terminal, and API management capabilities.

layers.name: App Core
layers.description: Root Angular application component, route definitions, HTTP interceptors, auto-save persistence, theme service, configuration providers, and dependency injection tokens that form the central application shell

layers.name: Feature Pages
layers.description: Top-level feature modules including project creation wizard, content editor workspace, application settings panel, user account management, and on-device AI chat interface via WebLLM

layers.name: Shared Components
layers.description: Reusable Angular component library including API explorer, draggable panels, context menus, modal dialogs, selection controls, tab groups, data tables, tree views, authorization UI, file picker, notebook editor with markdown and OpenAPI support, notification toasts, privacy error dialogs, server and service management panels, and terminal emulator

layers.name: Directives and Utilities
layers.description: Custom Angular structural and attribute directives (element ID, element index, highlight, unless, view scroll), shared data model classes, and example components used across the application

layers.name: Application Bootstrap
layers.description: Application entry points including custom element integration (Luxio), Angular platform bootstrap, server-side rendering entry with Express, polyfills, service worker background script, SVG sprite injection, inline styles, test harness entry, HTML templates, and TypeScript type declarations

layers.name: Configuration and Documentation
layers.description: Project-level configuration including Angular workspace settings, TypeScript compiler options across multiple targets, npm package manifest, PostCSS configuration, browser compatibility, development proxy settings, PWA manifest, UTM source tracking, Claude AI settings, Angular environment variables per deployment target, and project README documentation

layers.name: Assets and Infrastructure
layers.description: Global application stylesheets, SQL test data for development, build automation scripts, static asset configurations for microservice listings and ML chat models, custom library CSS, and tooling ignore files

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README introduces Luxio, an Angular-based web assistant application that combines an AI-powered chat interface, a code editor, a terminal emulator, and API management capabilities into a single workspace. It provides the high-level purpose and serves as a roadmap for understanding how the different layers of the application fit together, from the custom element entry point to the shared component library.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: The index.ts file is the public API for Luxio when consumed as a library. It exports the Luxio function that dynamically creates an app-root DOM element, injects global styles, and lazy-loads the Angular application bundle. This custom-element integration pattern allows third-party applications to embed the Luxio editor without needing to understand Angular bootstrapping details.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript lazy-loading with dynamic import() enables code splitting: the main Angular bundle is only loaded when Luxio() is called, keeping the initial payload small for embedding scenarios.

tour.title: Angular Application Bootstrap
tour.description: main.ts and main.common.ts work together to bootstrap the Angular application. main.ts loads persisted data from the Origin Private File System (OPFS), while main.common.ts configures the application with zoneless change detection, HttpClient with fetch API, server-side rendering hydration, and the custom configuration provider. The bootstrapApplication function with standalone component APIs is the modern Angular approach, avoiding NgModules entirely.
tour.languageLesson: Angular's standalone API (bootstrapApplication, provideZonelessChangeDetection) eliminates the need for NgModules. provideHttpClient with withFetch() uses the modern fetch API instead of XMLHttpRequest, enabling better performance and stream support.

tour.title: Root Application Component
tour.description: AppComponent is the root standalone Angular component that orchestrates the entire UI layout. It manages the tab system for opened editors, the resizable terminal panel, the side panel for file navigation, and drag-based panel resizing via mouse events on the host element. All feature components and shared UI elements are imported here, making this the central wiring point for the application shell.

tour.title: Core Services
tour.description: CoreService is the central hub of the application with over 70 methods handling API management, file operations, authentication state, upload tracking, and cross-component communication via Angular signals. ThemeService provides dark and light theme toggling with persistence to localStorage. Both services are provided at the root level and injected throughout the entire application by all feature and shared components.
tour.languageLesson: Angular signals (signal, computed, WritableSignal) provide fine-grained reactivity. The upload progress tracking uses WritableSignal for per-task progress and computed() to derive the overall percentage, enabling efficient template updates without change detection.

tour.title: Shared Data Models
tour.description: The model.ts file defines the core data types used across the entire codebase: AstTreeNode for file and server tree hierarchies, ServiceRouteInfo for API service routing, UserInfo for authentication, and DocModelType for document state. These classes and interfaces form the shared vocabulary that every component and service relies on for type-safe communication.

tour.title: Content Editor Workspace
tour.description: ContentComponent is the primary workspace with 65 methods managing the core editing experience. It orchestrates file tree navigation, tab management with drag-and-drop reordering, code editing panels, API exploration via the AstApiComponent, WebSocket-based file operations, and notebook rendering. This component depends on nearly every shared component in the library, making it the most complex integration point in the application.

tour.title: Feature Modules
tour.description: Three feature components extend the core workspace: AddProjectComponent is a project creation wizard with file tree and table UIs; SettingsComponent provides application configuration options; and WebllmComponent integrates the WebLLM library for on-device AI chat via Llama models running directly in the browser. Together they demonstrate how feature modules reuse the shared component library.
tour.languageLesson: WebLLM (CreateMLCEngine from @mlc-ai/web-llm) runs large language models entirely in-browser using WebGPU. The initProgressCallback pattern provides real-time model download and loading progress to the UI.

tour.title: Shared UI Component Library
tour.description: The shared UI library provides reusable building blocks assembled into feature panels. AstModalComponent provides overlay dialogs with configurable content. AstTabGroupComponent and AstTabComponent implement a tabbed panel system with context menus. AstTreeComponent renders hierarchical file and server trees with expand/collapse, rename, and drag operations. These components are the construction kit used by every feature module.

tour.title: Terminal Emulator
tour.description: The TerminalComponent provides an embedded terminal emulator within the application workspace. TerminalService manages the backend connection state and session lifecycle. The terminal integrates with the main app shell's resize system, supporting a draggable panel that can be toggled open and closed, providing a developer-friendly command-line interface alongside the code editor.

tour.title: Auto-Save Persistence
tour.description: AutoSaver implements debounced automatic saving using the Origin Private File System (OPFS) API via the opfs-tools library. It periodically serializes editor state at a configurable interval, ensuring user work is preserved without manual save actions. The save logic delegates to CoreService's queuedWrite function, demonstrating the layered architecture where utility classes depend on the core service layer.
tour.languageLesson: The debounced save pattern (setInterval with configurable ms) batches rapid changes into periodic writes. OPFS provides a high-performance file system API exclusive to the browser's origin, enabling near-native read/write speeds for editor persistence.

tour.title: Project Configuration
tour.description: The package.json declares the project's dependencies including Angular 18+, WebLLM for AI chat, opfs-tools for file persistence, and jsZip for archive operations. The angular.json file configures the Angular CLI workspace with separate build configurations for development, production, and server-side rendering. Together they define the toolchain that compiles, serves, and deploys the application.
